phase: Phase 3 smoke — estimator validation on synthetic SCM

true_effect.method: pulse simulation with common random numbers on a z-space replica of generate() (replica validated bit-for-bit against generate() with interventions off); +1 z pulse to fan_speed_nc at spaced times, failure_risk differenced at t+3
true_effect.observed_outcome_note: effect on the clipped engineering failure_risk (the outcome estimators see), same pulses; per +80 fan units before the /80 division

refuters.interpretation: PASS — adding a random common cause barely moves the estimate
PASS — permuted (fake) treatment collapses the effect to ~0, as it should if the real estimate is genuinely driven by the treatment
PASS — estimate is stable on an 80% data subset

estimator_vs_truth_notes: LinearDML (-0.06933/unit) and DoWhy linear regression (-0.07114/unit) agree closely with each other. Both are attenuated relative to the LATENT z-space pulse truth (-0.09581/unit), and the DML 95% CI excludes the latent truth. Part of the gap is mechanical: generate() clips the observed failure_risk to [0, 100], and the same pulses applied to the clipped observed outcome give -0.06529/unit — the like-for-like target for estimators fit on observed data. The remaining gap vs the observed-outcome truth is 0.00404/unit (candidate contributors: RandomForest nuisance shrinkage in LinearDML and the mild hpc_outlet_temp nonlinearity; not isolated in this smoke run).
